{{Quote|Here's my jump speeder, which hasn't been working right since I cleaned the repulsorlift coil. Aren't you supposed to clean it?|[[Ezra Bridger]] in his private journal|<ref name="Rebel Journal by Ezra Bridger">''[[Rebel Journal by Ezra Bridger]]''</ref>}}
The '''''Undicur''-class jumpspeeder''', also referred to as the '''Jedi jumpspeeder''', was a [[speeder bike]] manufactured by [[Kuat Vehicles]]. 

==Description==
[[File:Undicur-class_jumpspeeder_SWRFacebook.png|thumb|250px|left|Sabine Wren riding a jumpspeeder]]
A compact speeder bike, the ''Undicur''-class was designed to be sold alongside [[starship]]s as utility vehicles, local transportation, and search and rescue missions. Their durable frame, coupled with the low-output [[repulsorlift]] engines, made them easy to produce and stow aboard ships like the [[Eta-class shuttle|''Eta''-class shuttle]].<ref name="EV" /> Young rebel and [[Padawan|Jedi-in-training]] [[Ezra Bridger]] was unsure if an Undicur owner was supposed to clean its repulsorlift coil, citing how his speeder had not been working as it was supposed to since he had cleaned it.<ref name="Rebel Journal by Ezra Bridger" />

Collapsible, their simple saddle and control panel were sufficient for short trips between a starship and a destination. During the Clone Wars, the jumpspeeders saw frequent use by the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] and members of the [[Jedi Order]].<ref name="EV" />

==History==
[[File:AhsokaOffersObiWanALift-GoM.png|thumb|300px|right|Ahsoka Tano rode a jumpspeeder to rescue Obi-Wan Kenobi on Mortis.]]
Though designed as an emergency craft for the [[Jedi Order]] and regional military patrols, the design proved popular with civilians after the [[Clone Wars]].<ref name="Head2Head" /> Several were used by [[Jedi]] [[Jedi Master|Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], and [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] during the [[mission to Mortis]].<ref name="Ghosts" /> One was later used by [[Sabine Wren]] four [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Lothal]]<ref name="Call" /> a [[Raid near Jalath]].

[[Ezra Bridger]] and [[Kanan Jarrus]] rode a pair of ''Undicur''-class from [[Lando Calrissian's farm]] and saw the remains of a burned [[Lothal re-settlement camp 43|Tarkintown]].<ref name="The Siege of Lothal">''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Siege of Lothal]]''</ref> Sabine lent her bike to her friend [[Ketsu Onyo]], but she ended up destroying Sabine's speeder bike due to her carelessness.<ref name="Crash course">{{FOD|Crash Course}}</ref>

{{Veh-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Undicur''-class jumpspeeder was based on a vehicle concept by [[Joe Johnston]]<ref name="SW-Repurposed Star Wars Technology - Back from the Drawing Board, Part 2">{{SW|url=news/back-from-the-drawing-board-part-2-repurposed-star-wars-technology|text=Repurposed ''Star Wars'' Technology - Back from the Drawing Board, Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref> for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']]. It first appeared in "[[Ghosts of Mortis]]," the seventeenth episode of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' animated series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]], which aired on [[February 11]], [[2011]].<ref name="Ghosts of Mortis Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode317.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Ghosts of Mortis}}</ref>

It was first named as the ''Undicur''-class jumpspeeder in the [[2014]] reference book ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Head to Head]]'', authored by [[Pablo Hidalgo]].<ref name="Head2Head" /> In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, the name was first given in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]'', a 2011 reference book written by [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="Legends">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref>
